items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Frankie Newton in the context of Flip Phillips working with him, but the interviewee (Charlie Barnet) does not mention Frankie Newton personally or describe a direct relationship.

ctx.x: Leonard Feather, in, "The Book of Jazz," devotes some space to white bandleaders who hired black musicians, and there were so very, very few of them in the '30s and early '40s, and of course he gives you credit for having a mixed band, and he mentions the very few others, Artie Shaw having Billie Holiday in the band and Benny Goodman

having Teddy Wilson and Lionel Hampton, and Flip Phillips working with Frankie Newton. Let's see -- at Kelly Stables. But -- and Roy Eldridge, long association with Gene Krupa's big band. But this was something pretty rare during that period. Is that right? I mean --
Oh, yeah, it was rare all right. Although it actually -- I didn't do it to be revolutionary. It just -- it occurred to me as a wonderful idea. I said, "Why hasn't somebody done this?"
